channel.description: Source-grounded updates about AI, cognition and attention. Automated extracts are not expert-reviewed appraisals.

item.title: A Human-Centred Framework for Integrating Generative AI to Foster Critical Thinking, Learner Autonomy, and Cognitive Engagement in K-12 Education
item.description: Further research should evaluate the framework and examine measurable learning outcomes.

item.title: The impact of AI on students’ achievement, confidence, and critical thinking in education in Morocco
item.description: This paper examines the effects of AI use within the context of higher education institutions, as it investigates Moroccan postgraduate students’ perceptions on their academic achievements. This research follows a qualitative approach, as it aims to capture the students’ experience of AI use in their academic life.

item.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Cognitive Scaffolding, Substitution, and the Risk of Deskilling
item.description: This article argues that these findings can be understood by considering how cognitive work is distributed between users and AI systems and how this distribution may evolve over time. In particular, I examine a six-step sequence in which successful complementary assistance can increase trust and delegation; greater delegation can remain complementary or become increasingly…

item.title: Beyond AI Use: How AI Literacy Is Linked to Critical Thinking through AI-Assisted Problem-Solving Ability and AI Reliance
item.description: Quantitative results showed that AI literacy was positively associated with AI-assisted problem-solving ability and indirectly associated with critical thinking through AI-assisted problem-solving ability and AI reliance.

item.title: Digital attention disruption and academic impact in adolescents: a data-driven network and machine learning analysis
item.description: Results showed that LASSO regression identified stress level (coefficient = 0.384) and social media use duration (coefficient = 0.297) as the strongest predictors of academic impact. Network analysis revealed a three-community structure, corresponding to the “digital distraction load,” “psychological-academic exhaustion,” and “academic engagement” dimensions, with academic impact located at the intersection of the first two communities.

item.title: Algorithmic management and gig workers' workplace wellbeing: the moderating role of psychological resilience
item.description: We find that algorithmic management is positively associated with both challenge appraisal and threat appraisal. Challenge appraisal is positively associated with workplace wellbeing, whereas threat appraisal is negatively associated with workplace wellbeing.

item.title: AI in education: boosting productivity or challenging cognitive effort?
item.description: This study aims to examine how university students associate AI-led productivity gains with less study time, better grades, better understanding of study material, changes in cognitive effort they put into AI-supported task completion and dependency on AI tools. The observed differences between daily and weekly users, particularly in critical evaluation and perceived accuracy…

item.description: Notably, in the task-switching performance, the ID group demonstrated faster reaction times to sleep-related stimuli. fMRI results revealed altered activation in the right precuneus, angular gyrus, and superior temporal gyrus, with interaction effects between group and stimulus type. item.title: What is the Socratic method? Could it be used to test students in an age of AI?
item.description: Plato’s dialogues show that learning takes place through the to-and-fro of reflective thought – much of learning is finding out what we don’t know.

item.title: Here’s how a learning strategy can make AI work for you
item.description: Generative AI can make learning faster and easier, but that does not necessarily mean we are learning better.

item.title: Parental Notification Gaps in ChatGPT-5: An Empirical Study
item.description: Using an automated judge (with targeted human audit) and comparing the current backend to legacy variants (GPT-4.1/4o), we find that notifications are selective rather than comprehensive: privacy violence, fraud, hate speech, and malware triggered no parental alerts in our runs, whereas physical harm (highest), pornography, and some health queries produced intermittent alerts.

item.title: Between Human and Machine: University Teachers’ Accounts of Judgment, Metacognitive Defense, and Cognitive Offloading in Generative AI Use
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) allows university teachers to delegate cognitive work while deciding how students should engage with it. Using codebook thematic analysis, we examined multi-source accounts from 25 teachers recruited through an AI-focused learning community and its professional networks in China.

item.title: AI-Assisted Translation Pedagogy for Critical Thinking: A Pathway to Sustainable Education
item.description: The results show that while students frequently use AI for translation, writing, and language learning, their engagement remains primarily functional and efficiency-driven.

item.title: AI-MEDIATED WELLBEING SURVEILLANCE AND THE BOUNDARY OF PSYCHOLOGICAL SAFETY
item.description: This paper develops a conceptual model of how AI-mediated wellbeing monitoring reshapes psychological safety, the shared belief that a work environment is safe for interpersonal risk-taking on which voice, dissent and error reporting depend.

item.title: Exploring Digital Competence Configurations and Attention Performance Through fsQCA and Machine Learning

item.title: The Prisoner's Dilemma of AI: Cognitive Offloading Among Future Mathematics Teachers
item.description: This study compares pretest and posttest perceptions of generative AI among first-year pre-service mathematics teachers following a targeted educational intervention focused on principles of AI functioning and related cognitive risks.

item.title: Decision-Making in the Digital Age: Midbrain Dopaminergic Circuits, Prefrontal Control, and Cognitive Autonomy
item.description: Decision-making is an essential cognitive process for human survival and adaptation, supported by an intricate network that integrates prefrontal executive control, affective processing, and midbrain dopaminergic systems.The digital age has introduced unprecedented environmental pressures, including information overload, persuasive interface design, social validation cues…

item.title: THE INFLUENCE OF DIGITAL DISTRACTION ON UNIVERSITY STUDENTS' ENGLISH LEARNING
item.description: This article examines the influence of digital distraction on university students' English learning through an integrative review of recent international studies and research conducted in the context of Uzbekistan.

item.title: AI as Market Infrastructure: How Misinformation and Automation Inequality Shape Democratic Performance and Economic Wellbeing
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the market-organizing infrastructures that coordinate exchange, reshaping consumer information environments and the allocation of economic value. Drawing on marketing systems theory and consumer emancipation scholarship, we theorize perceived misinformation threat and perceived automation inequality as system-level diagnostics that…

item.title: AI-Driven Urge Regulation Assistant (AURA): Designing Preemptive Smart Wearables for Smoking Cessation
item.description: Through an iterative co-design interview process, we examine (1) the barriers and facilitators to smoking cessation and (2) the desired design features of wearable systems targeting cravings before lapses occur.

item.title: What happens to language when machines start talking back?
item.description: AI systems tend to focus on the person speaking – but the listener plays just as big a part in communication.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence as Cognitive Scaffolding for Executive Functioning in Students with Special Educational Needs
item.description: Research on executive functions, self-regulated learning, artificial intelligence in education, and special education was brought together to examine intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive platforms, planning tools, learning analytics, conversational agents, and generative AI. Some applications compensate for an executive demand, others scaffold performance while a task is…

item.title: Artificial Intelligence Usage, Cognitive Offloading, and Academic Performance among Rural Undergraduate Students: A Sequential Mediation Model
item.description: Findings suggest that unsupervised AI adoption elevates cognitive offloading, which erodes self-regulated learning and ultimately constrains academic performance perception, with academically weaker students disproportionately at risk.

item.title: An Investigation into AI Dependence, Critical Thinking and Writing Competence among Nigerian University Undergraduates
item.description: This study investigated the relationship between AI dependence and critical thinking and writing competence among English Language students. The study concluded that excessive dependence on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly and QuillBot is inversely associated with students' ability to analyze, evaluate and produce original written texts.

item.title: Cognitive Augmentation or Cognitive Offloading? Artificial Intelligence in Education and Lifelong Learning
item.description: This study integrates these domains through a common framework distinguishing cognitive augmentation, where AI supports human thinking, from cognitive offloading, where it substitutes for it. item.title: The Cognitive Debt of AI-Augmented Project Management: How Repeated Cognitive Offloading May Erode Professional Judgment and Project Resilience
item.description: This article introduces the concept of cognitive debt to explain this deferred capability cost in AI-augmented project management.

item.title: Augmentation or Erosion? Regulating Cognitive Offloading in Generative AI-Supported STEM Learning
item.description: This article develops an augmentation–erosion framework that accounts for part of this heterogeneity by treating the educational effect of GenAI not as a property of the tool but as a property of the partition of cognitive labor between learner and machine.
